metaDescription: Build an Nginx map block that flags selected user-agents, plus the server snippet that denies or rate-limits them. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Creates the map and the server snippet that block or limit bots by user-agent.
why:
The cleanest way to block bots in Nginx is a map on $http_user_agent that sets a variable, followed by one check in the server. It scales to long bot lists without chains of if statements.

List the tokens and choose block with a status code or rate limit with limit_req. The rate-limit variant uses an empty key for normal visitors so only flagged bots are limited.
howTo: Choose block or rate limit and the variable name.
Put the map in http {} and the rest in server {}.
Reload Nginx and test with curl -A.

faq.a: In the http block, not inside server.

faq.q: Why use map instead of if?
faq.a: map is evaluated once, and if inside server has well-known pitfalls.

faq.q: How does the rate limit skip normal visitors?
faq.a: Their key is an empty string, which limit_req does not count.
Yes, set the status code option.
